column3: The Hebrew presents taking refuge as a completed action; BSB uses the present.
The Hebrew has you said, feminine singular; BSB says I said.
The Hebrew names another in the singular without explicitly saying gods; it pictures names being lifted to the lips.
The Hebrew describes holding his lot rather than a completed making secure.
The Hebrew names kidneys rather than conscience and presents His counsel as completed.
The Hebrew names my glory rather than my tongue and my flesh rather than my body.
The Hebrew pictures seeing the pit; BSB says see decay.
The Hebrew uses an imperfect for making known and verbless descriptions of joys and pleasures; BSB says You have made known and You will fill me.
